sentences.en: This is a daily.
sentences.zh: 这是一个日常栏目。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天。

sentences.en: The prosecution's case so far in the closely watched trial of Derek Chauvin, the former Minneapolis police officer accused of murdering George Floyd.
sentences.zh: 在备受关注的前明尼阿波利斯警察德里克·沙文谋杀乔治·弗洛伊德案的审判中，控方迄今为止的案情陈述。

sentences.en: I spoke with my colleague, John Eligo, in Minneapolis.
sentences.zh: 我在明尼阿波利斯采访了我的同事约翰·埃利戈。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, April 8th.
sentences.zh: 今天是4月8日，星期四。

sentences.en: John, I wanted to start by having you set the scene there in Minneapolis this past week or so.
sentences.zh: 约翰，我想请你先介绍一下过去一周左右明尼阿波利斯的现场情况。

sentences.en: What are your impressions of this trial so far?
sentences.zh: 你对目前的这场审判有什么印象？

sentences.en: It's really a city on edge right now.
sentences.zh: 这里现在确实是一座处于边缘的城市。

sentences.en: I mean, you walk around downtown, there's cement barricades with fencing and barbed wire up.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你走在市中心，到处都是带铁丝网和栅栏的水泥路障。

sentences.en: There's National Guard armored vehicles and National Guard members who are standing outside watching over everything.
sentences.zh: 有国民警卫队的装甲车，还有国民警卫队队员站在外面巡视一切。

sentences.en: People are already starting to board up windows.
sentences.zh: 人们已经开始用木板封住窗户。

sentences.en: So there's clearly this underlying tension of, you know, what's going to happen with this trial?
sentences.zh: 因此，很显然存在这种潜在的紧张情绪，你知道的，这场审判会怎么样？

sentences.en: What's the verdict going to be?
sentences.zh: 判决会是什么？

sentences.en: And is that going to lead to more unrest like they saw last year when, you know, there was lots of vandalism and buildings burning amid, you know, mass protests for racial justice?
sentences.zh: 这会不会引发更多的骚乱，就像他们去年看到的那样，当时，你知道的，在争取种族公正的大规模抗议活动中，有很多打砸抢和建筑物着火的现象？

sentences.en: So you really get like around the town that this is something that cannot be avoided, that people cannot stop thinking about.
sentences.zh: 所以你真的能感觉到整个小镇都觉得这是一件无法避免的事情，人们无法停止思考。

sentences.en: And then you look, you know, in the courtroom now.
sentences.zh: 然后你看，你知道的，现在在法庭里。

sentences.en: And you have to look from afar, right?
sentences.zh: 你必须远远地看，对吧？

sentences.en: Because of COVID protocols, there's very few people allowed into the courtroom.
sentences.zh: 由于新冠疫情防控协议，只有极少数人被允许进入法庭。

sentences.en: As reporters, we're not even allowed in there.
sentences.zh: 作为记者，我们甚至不被允许进去。

sentences.en: We're allowed to have one person representing all print media, one person representing all broadcast media.
sentences.zh: 我们只被允许让一个人代表所有平面媒体，一个人代表所有广播媒体。

sentences.en: So I'm sitting here in my hotel room with, you know, a bag of chips and some bottled water watching this trial.
sentences.zh: 所以我正坐在我的酒店房间里，你知道的，手里拿着一袋薯片和一些瓶装水，看着这场审判。

sentences.en: And, you know, what's proceeding inside the courtroom?
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，法庭里面正在进行什么？

sentences.en: Honestly, Michael, it's like a range of emotions and impressions, I would say, because on the one hand, you have this video of
sentences.zh: 说实话，迈克尔，这就像是一系列的情绪和印象，我想说，因为一方面，你有这样一段视频

sentences.en: George Floyd's death playing over and over and over and over and over again during testimony in the courtroom.
sentences.zh: 在法庭的作证过程中，乔治·弗洛伊德死亡的画面一遍、一遍、一遍、一遍、又一遍地播放着。

sentences.en: So it's in many ways kind of like bringing that kind of trauma all to the surface again, right?
sentences.zh: 所以在很多方面，它就像是把那种创伤再次全部浮出水面，对吧？

sentences.en: So there's like that emotional part of it.
sentences.zh: 所以有那种感性的部分。

sentences.en: Then there's also like, it's a trial, right?
sentences.zh: 然后还有，这是一场审判，对吧？

sentences.en: It's technical.
sentences.zh: 它是技术性的。

sentences.en: They parse all these, you know, different legal nuances, all these medical nuances.
sentences.zh: 他们剖析所有这些，你知道的，不同的法律细微差别，所有这些医学细微差别。

sentences.en: And you're really seeing a battle develop inside the courtroom over fundamentally, what is this case about?
sentences.zh: 你确实看到法庭内部展开了一场关于根本问题的较量，这个案件到底是关于什么的？

sentences.en: For the prosecution, it's about that video, that nine minutes plus that you see
sentences.zh: 对控方来说，它是关于那段视频，也就是你看到的超过九分钟的时间里

sentences.en: Derek Chauvin kneeling on George Floyd's neck.
sentences.zh: 德里克·沙文用膝盖跪压在乔治·弗洛伊德的脖子上。

sentences.en: And then the defense is saying, no, no, no, it's not the video.
sentences.zh: 然后辩方说，不，不，不，不是那段视频。

sentences.en: It's all these other things.
sentences.zh: 是所有这些其他事情。

sentences.en: Don't just look at the video.
sentences.zh: 不要只看视频。

sentences.en: And so that's really the bad lines that have been drawn as you watch this trial each and every day.
sentences.zh: 所以，当你每天观看这场审判时，这就是真正划定的争论界限。

sentences.en: So let's talk about what you've been able to watch or piece together inside the courtroom as the prosecution has laid out its case and started to call witnesses.
sentences.zh: 那么我们来谈谈你所能看到或拼凑起来的法庭内部情况，当时控方陈述了案情并开始传唤证人。

sentences.en: Where should we start?
sentences.zh: 我们从哪里开始？

sentences.en: The heart of the case really is how did George Floyd die?
sentences.zh: 案件的核心其实是乔治·弗洛伊德是怎么死的？

sentences.en: Because the prosecution is attempting to show that he died because Derek Chauvin knelt on his neck for more than nine minutes, right?
sentences.zh: 因为控方正试图证明他是因为德里克·沙文在他的脖子上跪压了九多分钟而死的，对吧？

sentences.en: And so in order to do that, they have to have medical experts who can attest to that.
sentences.zh: 为了做到这一点，他们必须有能够证明这一点的医学专家。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: The state calls Dr. Bradford Langenfeld, John.
sentences.zh: 州方传唤了布拉德福德·兰根费尔德医生，约翰。
zh_words: 布拉德福德·兰根费尔德

sentences.en: And the one expert that we've seen who's probably said that most powerfully so far is the actual
sentences.zh: 我们见到的那位迄今为止最有力的专家，大概就是那位

sentences.en: emergency room doctor who pronounced George Floyd dead at the hospital and who treated him before he died.
sentences.zh: 在医院宣布乔治·弗洛伊德死亡并在他死前对他进行治疗的急诊室医生。

sentences.en: When Mr. Floyd's body, when Mr. Floyd was brought in, would you describe it as an emergency situation?
sentences.zh: 当弗洛伊德先生的遗体，当弗洛伊德先生被送进来时，你会把它描述为紧急情况吗？

sentences.en: Yes, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是的。

sentences.en: What was his condition in terms of his cardiac condition?
sentences.zh: 就他的心脏状况而言，他的情况如何？

sentences.en: He was in cardiac arreSt.
sentences.zh: 他心搏骤停。

sentences.en: He said essentially that when George Floyd came to him that his heart was already stopped.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是说，当乔治·弗洛伊德来到他这里时，他的心脏已经停止跳动了。

sentences.en: Mr. Floyd had been in arrest for, by this time, 60 minutes.
sentences.zh: 到这个时候，弗洛伊德先生已经心脏骤停了60分钟。

sentences.en: Yes, I determined that the likelihood of any meaningful outcome was far below 1% and that we would not be able to resuscitate Mr. Floyd.
sentences.zh: 是的，我确定任何有意义的结果的可能性都远低于1%，我们无法让弗洛伊德先生复苏。

sentences.en: And so I then pronounced him dead.
sentences.zh: 所以我随后宣布他死亡。

sentences.en: And he said that from all the signs that he had, all the information that he received, that in a nutshell, he did not have sufficient oxygen.
sentences.zh: 他说，根据他所有的迹象，他收到的所有信息，简而言之，他没有足够的氧气。

sentences.en: Was your leading theory then for the cause of Mr. Floyd's cardiac arrest, oxygen deficiency?
sentences.zh: 那么，你当时对弗洛伊德先生心脏骤停原因的主要推测是缺氧吗？

sentences.en: That was one of the more likely possibilities I felt.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这是更有可能性的情况之一。

sentences.en: And that lack of oxygen led to asphyxia and that essentially causes heart to fail and causes heart to stop.
sentences.zh: 而这种缺氧导致了窒息，这本质上导致心脏衰竭并导致心脏停止跳动。

sentences.en: And doctor, is there another name for death by oxygen deficiency?
sentences.zh: 医生，缺氧致死还有另一个名字吗？

sentences.en: Asphyxia is a commonly understood term.
sentences.zh: 窒息是一个普遍理解的词。

sentences.en: Thank you, Dr. Langanthal.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，兰根塔尔医生。

sentences.en: No further questions.
sentences.zh: 没有其他问题了。

sentences.en: And that's a very important point because, for one, the medical examiner who actually did the autopsy on George Floyd did not say asphyxiation is a cause of death.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常重要的点，因为一方面，实际对乔治·弗洛伊德进行尸检的法医并没有说窒息是死因。

sentences.en: He basically said that George Floyd's heart stopped.
sentences.zh: 他基本上说乔治·弗洛伊德的心脏停止了跳动。

sentences.en: And what the prosecution is trying to show is that it was the asphyxiation that led to that, while the defense, on the other hand, is trying to show that, hey, there were all
sentences.zh: 而控方试图证明的是，正是窒息导致了这一点，而辩方则试图证明，嘿，有所有

sentences.en: these reasons for George Floyd's heart stopping.
sentences.zh: 这些原因导致乔治·弗洛伊德的心脏停止跳动。

sentences.en: You know, one of them being his drug use, one of them being a lot of the adrenaline pumping through him.
sentences.zh: 你知道，其中之一是他的吸毒史，其中之一是体内涌动的大量肾上腺素。

sentences.en: So the defense is really trying to paint a holistic picture of George Floyd and his whole medical history and his drug use and things like that and use that to argue, while the
sentences.zh: 所以辩方确实在试图描绘一个全面的乔治·弗洛伊德，包括他的整个病史和吸毒史之类的事情，并以此来进行辩论，而

sentences.en: prosecution is saying, hey, no, it's asphyxiation that, but for the fact that Derek Chauvin knelt on his neck, George Floyd would be alive today.
sentences.zh: 控方则在说，嘿，不，这就是窒息，要不是德里克·沙文在他的脖子上跪压，乔治·弗洛伊德今天还活着。

sentences.en: So given that testimony, it feels like understanding whether or not Chauvin's actions were justified would also be crucial to the prosecution's case.
sentences.zh: 因此，鉴于这段证词，感觉理解沙文的行为是否合理对控方的案件也至关重要。

sentences.en: So how do they approach that?
sentences.zh: 那么他们是如何处理这一点的呢？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So once you get past, you know, the medical portion of it, you have to look at the policing portion, right?
sentences.zh: 所以一旦你过了医学部分，你就得看看警务部分，对吧？

sentences.en: Because there are times when police officers are allowed to use force, even deadly force, right?
sentences.zh: 因为有时警察被允许使用武力，甚至是致命武力，对吧？

sentences.en: And so the question was whether this was a case where Chauvin needed deadly force or at least needed the force that he was using, which was kneeling on George Floyd's neck.
sentences.zh: 所以问题是，这是一个沙文需要致命武力，或者至少需要他正在使用的武力（即跪在乔治·弗洛伊德的脖子上）的案件吗？

sentences.en: And the prosecutors, they brought in several members of the police department to talk about
sentences.zh: 检察官们请来了警察局的几名成员来谈论

sentences.en: this from the longest serving homicide detective in the department all the way up to the police chief.
sentences.zh: 这一点，从局里资历最深的凶杀案侦探一直到警察局长。

sentences.en: So the man who's leading the department.
sentences.zh: 也就是领导这个部门的人。

sentences.en: So tell me about this longest serving officer from the Minneapolis Police Department.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲这位来自明尼阿波利斯警察局的资历最深的警官吧。

sentences.en: What was his testimony?
sentences.zh: 他的证词是什么？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So this was Lieutenant Richard Zimmerman.
sentences.zh: 这就是理查德·齐默尔曼中尉。

sentences.en: What is your view of that use of force during that time period?
sentences.zh: 你对这段时间内武力的使用有什么看法？

sentences.en: Totally unnecessary.
sentences.zh: 完全没有必要。

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 你是什么意思？

sentences.en: Well, first of all, pulling him down to the ground, face down, and putting your knee on the neck for that amount of time is just uncalled for.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，把他拉倒在地上，面朝下，把膝盖放在脖子上那么长时间，根本是毫无理由的。

sentences.en: I saw no reason why the officers felt they were in danger, if that's what they felt.
sentences.zh: 我看不出有什么理由让警察觉得他们处于危险之中，如果那是他们的感觉的话。

sentences.en: And that's what they would have to feel to be able to use that kind of force.
sentences.zh: 而为了能够使用那种武力，他们必须有这种感觉。

sentences.en: And what the defense has tried to argue is that, hey, these situations are uncertain.
sentences.zh: 辩方试图争辩说，嘿，这些情况是不确定的。

sentences.en: Even when individuals go unconscious, there's chances that they can, you know, wake back up and then become even more aggressive again.
sentences.zh: 即使在个人失去知觉时，也有可能，你知道，他们会再次醒来，然后变得更具攻击性。

sentences.en: But what Zimmerman essentially said was that when you have someone in handcuffs, as George
sentences.zh: 但齐默尔曼基本上说的是，当你有戴着手铐的人时，就像乔治·

sentences.en: Floyd was, the real threat that they pose goes way down.
sentences.zh: 弗洛伊德那样，他们构成的真正威胁大大降低。

sentences.en: Based on your review of the body cams, did you see any need for Officer Chauvin to improvise by putting his knee on Mr. Floyd for nine minutes and 29 seconds?
sentences.zh: 根据你对随身摄像头的审查，你看到沙文警官有任何必要通过将膝盖放在弗洛伊德先生身上九分二十九秒来进行权宜之计吗？

sentences.en: No, I did not.
sentences.zh: 不，我没有。

sentences.en: And then we get the top official of all.
sentences.zh: 然后我们迎来了最的高官员。

sentences.en: Your Honor, the state calls Chief Mederia Arredondo.
sentences.zh: 法官大人，州方传唤梅德里亚·阿雷多多局长。

sentences.en: Police Chief Mederia Arredondo, who is the head of the department.
sentences.zh: 警察局长梅德里亚·阿雷多多，他是该部门的负责人。

sentences.en: He is a Black man and the first Black police chief the city has ever had.
sentences.zh: 他是一名黑人，也是该市历史上第一位黑人警察局长。

sentences.en: And he took to the stand and essentially says that what Derek Chauvin did, not only was it not in line with department policy.
sentences.zh: 他走上证人席，基本上说德里克·沙文所做的事情，不仅不符合部门政策。

sentences.en: Do you believe that the defendant followed departmental policy 5-304 regarding de-escalation?
sentences.zh: 你认为被告是否遵循了关于降级冲突的5-304部门政策？

sentences.en: I absolutely do not agree with that.
sentences.zh: 我绝对不同意这一点。

sentences.en: They said it wasn't part of the department's ethics or values.
sentences.zh: 他们说这不是部门道德或价值观的一部分。

sentences.en: And clearly, when Mr. Floyd was no longer responsive and even motionless, to continue to apply that
sentences.zh: 很明显，当弗洛伊德先生不再有反应甚至一动不动时，继续对一个俯卧、

sentences.en: level of force to a person proned out, handcuffed behind their back, that in no way, shape, or
sentences.zh: 双手被反铐在背后的人施加那种程度的武力，在任何情况下、以任何方式或

sentences.en: form is anything that is by policy, is not part of our training, and it is certainly not part of our ethics or our values.
sentences.zh: 形式，都不是政策所允许的，不是我们训练的一部分，当然也不是我们道德或价值观的一部分。

sentences.en: So this was a stinging rebuke, essentially, of the actions of Derek Chauvin not acting as a Minneapolis police officer should ethically or morally.
sentences.zh: 因此，这基本上是对德里克·沙文没有按照明尼阿波利斯警察应有的道德或伦理行事的行为的严厉谴责。

sentences.en: I have a sense that police officers, let alone police chiefs, don't testify against their own
sentences.zh: 我有这样一种感觉，警察，更不用说警察局长了，不会轻易在警察队伍中指证自己的

sentences.en: colleagues on a police force lightly, and that it's quite rare for the leadership of a police department to be so openly critical of an officer.
sentences.zh: 同事，而且警察局领导层如此公开地批评一名警官是非常罕见的。

sentences.en: Or are we right to see this as quite unusual?
sentences.zh: 或者我们认为这很不寻常是对的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it is certainly unusual.
sentences.zh: 是的，这确实很不寻常。

sentences.en: I mean, it's very stunning to have a police chief rebuke an officer in his department like that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，警察局长这样公开斥责他部门里的警官是非常震撼的。

sentences.en: So I think for this police chief, it was also about setting a tone that I will defend my department, but when officers do wrong, I also have to speak up.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为对于这位警察局长来说，这也是为了定下一个基调，即我会捍卫我的部门，但当警察做错事时，我也必须大声说出来。

sentences.en: And some people I talked to afterward said it was refreshing to hear a police chief do that,
sentences.zh: 我事后采访的一些人说，听到警察局长这样做令人耳目一新，

sentences.en: and it was important in that they hope it could send some sort of broader message to other police
sentences.zh: 而且这很重要，因为他们希望这能向其他警察局长和

sentences.en: chiefs and other leadership of police departments that when your officers do wrong, you will actually speak up and call it out.
sentences.zh: 警察局的其他领导层传递某种更广泛的信息，即当你们的警察做错事时，你们真的会大声说出来并予以谴责。

sentences.en: But I imagine that for the jury, there's a lot of power in hearing the police chief say those things.
sentences.zh: 但我想对于陪审团来说，听到警察局长说这些话具有很大的力量。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对的。

sentences.en: I mean, this is the boss saying these things.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是老板在说这些话。

sentences.en: So that is going to carry a certain weight.
sentences.zh: 所以这会有一定的分量。

sentences.en: This is clearly a man who likes the police department, likes police officers, but he still thinks that this police officer was wrong.
sentences.zh: 这显然是一个热爱警察部门、热爱警察的人，但他仍然认为这个警察错了。

sentences.en: This is a city that is completely divided over its police department.
sentences.zh: 这是一座对其警察部门存在严重分裂的城市。

sentences.en: This is a city where many people are frustrated about policing and believe that what Derek Chauvin did is representative of a larger problem of abusive policing.
sentences.zh: 这是一个许多人对警务工作感到沮丧，并认为德里克·沙文所做的是滥用职权的更广泛问题的一个缩影的城市。

sentences.en: And so I think especially the chief's testimony was really a strong statement to the community as much as it was to the jury.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，特别是局长的证词，对社区而言，就像对陪审团一样，是一个强有力的声明。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.zh: 已解锁？

sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能访问所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你可以免费试用《时报》一个月，而不需要输入信用卡，会怎么样呢？

sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: John, beyond having police officials deliver testimony and condemnation of what Derek Chauvin
sentences.zh: 约翰，除了让警察官员发表证词和谴责德里克·沙文所

sentences.en: did, my sense is that the prosecution wanted there to be strong testimony from non-police figures who had seen what happened on May 25th of last year.
sentences.zh: 做的事情之外，我的感觉是控方希望那些亲眼目睹去年5月25日发生的事情的非警察人物也能提供强有力的证词。

sentences.en: Yeah, a big part of the prosecution's case so far has been to bring in this group of people who were just going about their everyday lives.
sentences.zh: 是的，控方迄今为止案情的一个重要部分就是把这群过着日常生活的人带到法庭上。

sentences.en: You know, they were going to, you know, buy snacks, going to fill up their tank of gas, going to buy a phone cord, who all converged on this corner in South Minneapolis.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们去买零食，去加满油箱，去买手机线，所有这些人汇聚在南明尼阿波利斯的这个街角。

sentences.en: You know, people from different walks of life, you know, people, you know, from nine years old to 61 years old, people who were there that day who witnessed it firsthand and saw
sentences.zh: 你知道的，来自各行各业的人，你知道的，从9岁到61岁的人，那天在那里亲眼目睹了这一切并看到了

sentences.en: what happened to George Floyd.
sentences.zh: 乔治·弗洛伊德遭遇的人。

sentences.en: And that really brought out some scenes of just astonishingly emotional testimony.
sentences.zh: 这确实带来了一些令人震惊的情感丰富的证词场景。

sentences.en: I mean, you had people who were standing feet away, who were yelling at the officers, who were interacting with the officers.
sentences.zh: 我是说，当时有几个人就站在几英尺外，对警察大喊大叫，与警察发生互动。

sentences.en: And these would become like the first eyewitnesses to this trauma that we would all kind of collectively watch and share around the world.
sentences.zh: 而这些人成为了这场创伤的第一批目击者，我们所有人在全世界范围内共同观看并分享了这些。

sentences.en: And who were these people?
sentences.zh: 这些都是什么人呢？

sentences.en: So one of the people that they called was this young man named Christopher Martin.
sentences.zh: 他们传唤的一个人名叫克里斯托弗·马丁。

sentences.en: C-H-R-I-S-T-O-P-H-E-R, last name Martin, M-A-R-T-I-N.
sentences.zh: C-H-R-I-S-T-O-P-H-E-R，姓马丁，M-A-R-T-I-N。

sentences.en: Mr. Martin, how old are you?
sentences.zh: 马丁先生，你今年多大？

sentences.en: Now, he worked at the store Cup Foods where this happened.
sentences.zh: 他曾在事发的Cup Foods便利店工作。

sentences.en: And Christopher, he was the person who interacted with George Floyd and actually sold him a pack of cigarettes and took a $20 bill that turned out to be a fake bill.
sentences.zh: 克里斯托弗就是与乔治·弗洛伊德互动、卖给他一包香烟并收下一张后来被发现是假币的20美元钞票的那个人。

sentences.en: And so it was Christopher Martin who first kind of reported to his boss that, hey, you know, I think this is a fake.
sentences.zh: 所以，是克里斯托弗·马丁第一个向他的老板汇报说，嘿，你知道的，我觉得这是一张假币。

sentences.en: And the boss sent Christopher out there to try to get George Floyd to come back in.
sentences.zh: 老板派克里斯托弗出去，试图让乔治·弗洛伊德再进店里来。

sentences.en: He didn't come back in.
sentences.zh: 他没有再进来。

sentences.en: The boss sent him out a second time with some of the other co-workers.
sentences.zh: 老板和其他几个同事一起第二次派他出去。

sentences.en: And they all tried to get George Floyd to come back in.
sentences.zh: 他们都试图让乔治·弗洛伊德进来。

sentences.en: He didn't come back in.
sentences.zh: 他没有进来。

sentences.en: And from there, the manager said, hey, we'll call the police.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，经理说，嘿，我们报警吧。

sentences.en: And so that's kind of like what started this series of events.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是引发这一系列事件的导火索。

sentences.en: And one thing that was very evident with Christopher Martin was this just burning sense of regret.
sentences.zh: 克里斯托弗·马丁身上非常明显的一点是，他有着一种强烈的负罪感。

sentences.en: You can actually see these moments in some of the surveillance footage where Christopher Martin's outside as George Floyd is being pinned to the ground with the knee on his neck.
sentences.zh: 你实际上可以在一些监控录像中看到这些时刻：当乔治·弗洛伊德被膝盖压住脖子按倒在地时，克里斯托弗·马丁正站在外面。

sentences.en: You could see him kind of pacing.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到他在焦急地踱步。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: You saw you standing there with your hands on your head for a while, correct?
sentences.zh: 你看到你当时双手抱头站在那里有一会儿，对吗？

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: What was going through your mind during that time period?
sentences.zh: 在那段时间里，你心里在想些什么？

sentences.en: Disbelief.
sentences.zh: 难以置信。

sentences.en: And guilt.
sentences.zh: 还有内疚。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Why guilt?
sentences.zh: 为什么会内疚？

sentences.en: If I would have just not taken the bill, this could have been avoided.
sentences.zh: 如果我当时没有收下那张钞票，这一切本可以避免。

sentences.en: And so it seems like he's haunted by his actions that day and what role they may have played in George Floyd's ultimate passing.
sentences.zh: 因此，他似乎一直被自己当天的行为以及这些行为在乔治·弗洛伊德最终离世中可能扮演的角色所困扰。

sentences.en: And how does that serve the prosecution's case?
sentences.zh: 这对于控方的案子有什么帮助呢？

sentences.en: His regret, his remorse, his description of his actions that day?
sentences.zh: 他的懊悔、他的内疚、他对当天自己行为的描述？

sentences.en: Well, I think you have to take the totality of his testimony into account, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为你必须把他的整体证词综合起来看，对吧？

sentences.en: So not only did he offer that testimony for the prosecution about his remorse and regret, but he also talked about what things looked like when George Floyd walked in.
sentences.zh: 因此，他不仅为控方提供了关于他内疚和懊悔的证词，他还讲述了乔治·弗洛伊德走进来时的情景。

sentences.en: They actually played surveillance footage of George Floyd in the store walking around.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至播放了乔治·弗洛伊德在店里四处走动的监控录像。

sentences.en: He seemed very friendly, approachable.
sentences.zh: 他看起来非常友好、平易近人。

sentences.en: He was talkative.
sentences.zh: 他很爱说话。

sentences.en: He seemed to just be having an average Memorial Day, just living his life.
sentences.zh: 他看起来只是在过一个普通的阵亡将士纪念日，过着他自己的生活。

sentences.en: But he did seem high.
sentences.zh: 但他确实看起来有点嗨。

sentences.en: He said, yeah, George Floyd appeared a little bit high, but he was otherwise coherent.
sentences.zh: 他说，是的，乔治·弗洛伊德看起来有点嗨，但除此之外他意识很清醒。

sentences.en: He was joking with people and things like that.
sentences.zh: 他在和别人开玩笑之类的。

sentences.en: So it was in some ways to bring George Floyd to life as like a human being who was going about his day that day.
sentences.zh: 所以在某种程度上，这是为了让乔治·弗洛伊德鲜活起来，让他成为一个正在过自己日子的有血有肉的人。

sentences.en: So I think that that's one of the important points.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得这是重要的一点。

sentences.en: And I think the other important point with Christopher and some of the other witnesses that we heard from is,
sentences.zh: 我认为克里斯托弗以及我们听取证词的其他目击者的另一个重要点在于，

sentences.en: I think in some ways, it's a reminder of how disproportionate Derek Chauvin's response was.
sentences.zh: 我认为在某种程度上，它提醒了人们德里克·沙文的反应是多么不成比例。

sentences.en: Because essentially, you had this, you know, at the time, 18-year-old who saw what George Floyd did is wrong, not the thing that, you know, he was supposed to do.
sentences.zh: 因为本质上，你有一个，你知道的，当时18岁的年轻人，他认为乔治·弗洛伊德做的事是错的，这不是他，你知道的，本该做的事。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But not something that warranted guns-drawn police response, you know, pinning him to the ground and kind of holding him down.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是那种需要全副武装的警察做出反应，你知道的，把他按倒在地并进行压制的行为。

sentences.en: So I think that is definitely an element that the prosecutors want to put out there about how disproportionate Derek Chauvin's response was.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得这绝对是检察官想要表达的一个要素，即德里克·沙文的反应是多么地过度和不成比例。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So who else is called to the stand who witnessed what happened as an eyewitness?
sentences.zh: 那么，还有谁被传唤出庭作证，作为目击了发生的一切的目击证人呢？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So we also had Darnella Frazier.
sentences.zh: 我们还有达内拉·弗雷泽。

sentences.en: Good morning, Darnella.
sentences.zh: 早上好，达内拉。

sentences.en: Good morning.
sentences.zh: 早上好。

sentences.en: Are you a little nervous up there?
sentences.zh: 你在上面有点紧张吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Who is the young woman, she was 17 at the time, who took that infamous bystander video that was posted to Facebook.
sentences.zh: 这位年轻女性当时17岁，她拍摄了那段发布到脸书上的、臭名昭著的路人视频。

sentences.en: And so she was actually with her nine-year-old cousin that day.
sentences.zh: 那天她实际上和她九岁的表弟在一起。

sentences.en: They were walking to the store to get snacks.
sentences.zh: 他们正步行去商店买零食。

sentences.en: And then Darnella mentions kind of seeing out of the corner of her eye, like this kind of police commotion going on in the street.
sentences.zh: 然后达内拉提到，她用眼角余光看到街上似乎有某种警察引发的骚乱。

sentences.en: When you walk past the squad car there, did you see anything happening there on the ground as you were walking towards Cup Foods with your cousin?
sentences.zh: 当你走过那辆警车时，你和表弟走向Cup Foods的时候，你看到地上有什么事情发生吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I see a man on the ground and I see a cop kneeling down on him.
sentences.zh: 我看到一个男人趴在地上，看到一个警察跪在他身上。

sentences.en: Was there anything about the scene that you didn't want your cousin to see?
sentences.zh: 现场有什么东西是你不想让你表弟看到的吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And what was that?
sentences.zh: 那是什么？

sentences.en: A man terrified, scared, begging for his life.
sentences.zh: 一个惊恐万分、害怕、祈求保命的男人。

sentences.en: And so she quickly ushers her cousin into the store and then comes back out.
sentences.zh: 于是她赶紧把表弟领进店里，然后又走了出来。

sentences.en: She took out her cell phone and hit record like, you know, so many people do.
sentences.zh: 她掏出手机开始录像，就像你知道的，很多人做的那样。

sentences.en: So tell the jury what you observed, what you heard, when you stopped to look at what was happening there at the scene.
sentences.zh: 所以请告诉陪审团，当你停下来观看现场发生的事情时，你观察到了什么，听到了什么。

sentences.en: I heard George Floyd saying, I can't breathe, please get off of me.
sentences.zh: 我听到乔治·弗洛伊德说，我喘不过气了，请从我身上下来。

sentences.en: I can't breathe.
sentences.zh: 我喘不过气了。

sentences.en: He cried for his mom.
sentences.zh: 他呼唤着他的妈妈。

sentences.en: He was in pain.
sentences.zh: 他很痛苦。

sentences.en: It seemed like he knew.
sentences.zh: 看起来他意识到了。

sentences.en: It seemed like he knew it was over for him.
sentences.zh: 看起来他知道自己快要不行了。

sentences.en: And much like Christopher Martin, Darnell also spoke to a real regret and sadness for what she witnessed.
sentences.zh: 和克里斯托弗·马丁一样，达内拉也对她目睹的一切表达了真正的懊悔和悲伤。

sentences.en: When I look at George Floyd, I look at, I look at my dad.
sentences.zh: 当我看着乔治·弗洛伊德时，我想到了，我想到了我的爸爸。

sentences.en: I look at my brothers.
sentences.zh: 我想到了我的兄弟们。

sentences.en: I look at my cousins, my uncles, because they are all black.
sentences.zh: 我想到了我的表亲、我的叔叔，因为他们都是黑人。

sentences.en: And I look at that and I look at how that could have been one of them.
sentences.zh: 我看着那个画面，想着那也可能是他们中的任何一个。

sentences.en: It's been nights.
sentences.zh: 有很多个夜晚。

sentences.en: I stayed up apologizing and apologizing to George Floyd for not doing more and not physically interacting and not saving his life.
sentences.zh: 我彻夜难眠，不断地、不断地向乔治·弗洛伊德道歉，因为我没有做更多的事，没有上前制止并救他的命。

sentences.en: And you could definitely tell that this is something that completely stays with her.
sentences.zh: 你绝对可以看得出来，这件事深深地烙印在她心里，挥之不去。

sentences.en: That, yes, her recording was a big deal for her to do that.
sentences.zh: 是的，她拍摄视频是一件很了不起的事。

sentences.en: But she felt like, looking back on it, it wasn't enough because it did not save George Floyd's life.
sentences.zh: 但回过头来看，她觉得这还远远不够，因为这并没有拯救乔治·弗洛伊德的生命。

sentences.en: And that was extremely powerful.
sentences.zh: 这极其震撼人心。

sentences.en: But that guilt is so complicated because, of course, what exactly were these witnesses supposed to have done?
sentences.zh: 但这种负罪感是如此复杂，因为当然了，这些目击者到底本该做些什么呢？

sentences.en: If you walk up to a police officer in the middle of an arrest and touch them or challenge them, you yourself could very easily get arrested for interfering in their work.
sentences.zh: 如果你在逮捕过程中走近警察并触碰他们或质疑他们，你自己很容易就会因为妨碍公务而被捕。

sentences.en: And so there's something very poignant and painful about watching these witnesses say they feel guilty when it's not really clear what they could have done differently.
sentences.zh: 因此，看着这些目击者说他们感到内疚，而又不太清楚他们究竟能做些什么改变，这种感觉非常凄凉和痛苦。

sentences.en: It really raises these questions of, like, what it's like to be a bystander in these situations and who can police the police.
sentences.zh: 这确实引发了这样一些问题：在这种情况下作为一个旁观者是怎样的体验，又是谁来监督警察。

sentences.en: Because police are the ones are supposed to be the ones who are supposed to stop wrong from happening in some ways.
sentences.zh: 因为警察本该是那些在某种程度上阻止不法行为发生的人。

sentences.en: But when you see a wrong happening and you think it's the police who are doing the wrong, yeah, you can litigate it after the fact,
sentences.zh: 但当你看到不法行为发生，而你认为作恶的正是警察时，是的，你事后可以去打官司，

sentences.en: but that's not going to save a life in the moment.
sentences.zh: 但这并不能在当下拯救一条生命。

sentences.en: And I think that that's the burden that people like Darnella carries with them for the rest of their lives, really.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是像达内拉这样的人余生都不得不背负的沉重负担。

sentences.en: Was there testimony from anyone who did seek to intervene in a meaningful way?
sentences.zh: 有没有证词来自那些确实试图以某种有意义的方式进行干预的人？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, there were several eyewitnesses there who in one shape or form did become a little bit more forceful in their efforts to intervene.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，现场有几位目击者，他们以某种形式在干预的努力上变得更加强硬了一些。

sentences.en: A full name is Donald William Williams II.
sentences.zh: 全名是唐纳德·威廉姆斯二世。

sentences.en: Specifically, I'm thinking of Donald WilliaMs.
sentences.zh: 具体来说，我想到的是唐纳德·威廉姆斯。

sentences.en: I'm an entrepreneur and a professional fighter.
sentences.zh: 我是一名企业家和职业格斗手。

sentences.en: He is actually a mixed martial arts fighter.
sentences.zh: 他实际上是一名综合格斗选手。

sentences.en: And he had went to the store that day to cup foods.
sentences.zh: 那天他去了那家商店，Cup Foods。

sentences.en: And you can see in the video, Donald Williams, he is extremely animated.
sentences.zh: 你可以在视频中看到，唐纳德·威廉姆斯情绪非常激动。

sentences.en: You can get him off the ground, you're being a bum right now.
sentences.zh: 你可以把他从地上拉起来，你现在像个无赖一样。

sentences.en: Were you here the whole time?
sentences.zh: 你当时一直在场吗？

sentences.en: Both, you know, in the bystander video that Darnella took, but also body camera footage that was played.
sentences.zh: 无论是在达内拉拍摄的路人视频中，还是在播放的随身执法记录仪视频中。

sentences.en: At one point he yells at Derek Chauvin that he was doing a blood choke.
sentences.zh: 他一度对德里克·沙文大喊大叫，说他在使用血锁（blood choke）。

sentences.en: Okay, we're done.
sentences.zh: 好了，我们完了。

sentences.en: So by the end of all of this eyewitness testimony, the message to the jury from the prosecution would seem to be that for all of these people,
sentences.zh: 所以在所有这些目击者证词结束时，控方给陪审团的信息似乎是，对于所有这些人来说，

sentences.en: there is absolutely no ambiguity that what they witnessed was wrong.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，他们亲眼目睹的事情是错误的。

sentences.en: And the depth of that feeling is clearly encapsulated by the trauma and the hauntedness that they're expressing.
sentences.zh: 这种感觉的深度清楚地体现在他们所表达的创伤和挥之不去的阴影中。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: How does the defense, then, do they try to rebut what these witnesses have observed and communicated in this testimony?
sentences.zh: 那么辩方是怎么做的呢，他们试图反驳这些证人在证词中所观察到并传达的内容吗？

sentences.en: What the defense does is they basically try to reframe this whole view of what the bystanders were doing.
sentences.zh: 辩方所做的是，他们基本上试图重新构建对旁观者所作所为的整套看法。

sentences.en: They portray them not as people who were desperate to help George Floyd, but as an angry mob that was threatening police officers.
sentences.zh: 他们把这些人描绘成不是急于帮助乔治·弗洛伊德的人，而是一群威胁警察的愤怒暴徒。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 嗨。

sentences.en: Just have some follow-up questions for you.
sentences.zh: 有些后续问题想问你。

sentences.en: And he even, you know, went after Genefieve Hansen, one of the witnesses who was there.
sentences.zh: 他甚至，你知道的，去质问了在场的证人之一杰内维芙·汉森。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: This is the fire, this is the firefighter.
sentences.zh: 这是消防，这是消防员。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: So he asked the firefighter, you know, why were you getting so upset?
sentences.zh: 所以他问那个消防员，你知道的，你为什么那么心烦意乱？

sentences.en: Like, why were you growing so angry?
sentences.zh: 比如，你为什么会变得这么生气？

sentences.zh: 你同意你自己的表现变得更大声、更沮丧、更不安吗？

sentences.en: Um, frustrated, I'm not sure is the word I would use.
sentences.zh: 嗯，沮丧，我不太确定这是我会用的词。

sentences.en: Angry?
sentences.zh: 生气？

sentences.en: More desperate.
sentences.zh: 更加绝望。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I got quite angry after Mr. Floyd was loaded into the ambulance and...
sentences.zh: 弗洛伊德先生被抬上救护车后，我变得非常生气，然后……

sentences.en: You yourself were saying, you know, vulgar things to the officer.
sentences.zh: 你自己在对警官说一些，你知道的，粗俗的话。

sentences.zh: 难道这群人不是越来越生气吗，因为他想把这个观点讲透？

sentences.en: And some people were yelling louder than others, right?
sentences.zh: 有些人喊得比其他人更大声，对吧？

sentences.en: Right.

sentences.en: And would you describe other people's demeanors as upset or angry?

sentences.en: Um, it's...
sentences.zh: 嗯，这……

sentences.zh: 我不知道你有没有见过别人被杀，但这确实令人心烦意乱。

sentences.en: So while the prosecution is presenting these eyewitnesses as evidence of how terribly wrong this all went and how guilty Derek Chauvin is,
sentences.zh: 因此，当控方将这些目击者作为证据，证明这一切错得多么离谱以及德里克·沙文多么有罪时，

sentences.en: is the defense is trying to make the case that that feeling among the witnesses and their reaction on the scene to try to intervene,
sentences.zh: 辩方是否在试图证明，证人之间的这种感觉以及他们在现场试图进行干预的反应，

sentences.en: that dynamic is what made Chauvin's behavior, they say, justified?
sentences.zh: 他们说，正是这种动态使得沙文的行为变得正当？

sentences.en: They say that the people gathered there made Chauvin feel or sense that there was a threat.
sentences.zh: 他们说，聚集在那里的人让沙文感到或感觉到存在威胁。

sentences.en: And because of that, he was not able to carry out his duties.
sentences.zh: 正因为如此，他无法履行职责。

sentences.en: He was not able to care for George Floyd because he perceived a threat.
sentences.zh: 由于他感知到了威胁，他无法照顾乔治·弗洛伊德。

sentences.en: And he was trying to maintain his own safety and the safety of others.
sentences.zh: 他当时在试图维护他自己和他人的安全。

sentences.en: And he was distracted from George Floyd, essentially.
sentences.zh: 从本质上讲，他被乔治·弗洛伊德的事情给分散了注意力。

sentences.en: Well, that's interesting, John.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这很有趣，约翰。

sentences.en: Are they then conceding, these defense lawyers, that Chauvin did something wrong or didn't do it properly?
sentences.zh: 这些辩护律师是在承认沙文做错了什么，或者没有做好吗？

sentences.en: I don't know if I'd say they're conceding that, per se.
sentences.zh: 我不知道我是不是会说他们本身在承认这一点。

sentences.en: But one of the charges is manslaughter, which is the lowest charge, which for Derek Chauvin would probably be, you know, short of an acquittal.
sentences.zh: 但其中一项指控是过失杀人，这是最低的指控，对德里克·沙文来说，可能，你知道的，差一点就无罪释放了。

sentences.en: That would be the best outcome for him, the lowest charge.
sentences.zh: 那对他来说会是最好的结果，最低的指控。

sentences.en: And in manslaughter, it requires some element of recklessness.
sentences.zh: 而在过失杀人中，它需要某种鲁莽的成分。

sentences.en: So you could reasonably see an argument in which he was a little bit reckless because of this commotion around him.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以合理地看到这样一种论点，即由于他周围的这种骚乱，他有一点鲁莽。

sentences.en: It caused him in some way to panic or to not act in the most proper of ways because of this commotion around him, right?
sentences.zh: 由于他周围的这种骚乱，在某种程度上导致他恐慌或者没有以最恰当的方式行事，对吧？

sentences.en: So this is an admittedly difficult question.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个公认很困难的问题。

sentences.en: But having watched all this testimony so closely, which version of this argument about the eyewitnesses do you think may have landed more forcefully with the jury,
sentences.zh: 但仔细观看了所有这些证词后，你认为关于目击者的这种论点的哪个版本可能在陪审团那里留下了更深刻的印象，

sentences.en: the prosecution or the defense?
sentences.zh: 控方还是辩方？

sentences.en: I know you said at the beginning of our conversation that you can't exactly read the room and the jury given the circumstances of how this trial is being carried out.
sentences.zh: 我知道你在我们对话开始时说过，鉴于这场审判的进行方式，你无法确切地揣摩现场氛围和陪审团的心思。

sentences.en: But I wonder what your sense of that is.
sentences.zh: 但我很好奇你对此有什么感觉。

sentences.en: I think that anyone who watches those bystanders and their reaction to what they saw that day cannot help but be moved by that.
sentences.zh: 我认为任何看到那些旁观者以及他们对那天所见所闻的反应的人，都不可避免地会被其触动。

sentences.en: If I'm not mistaken, I'm pretty sure of all the bystanders, there were probably two that did not cry.
sentences.zh: 如果我没记错的话，我很确信在所有的旁观者中，大概只有两个人没有哭。

sentences.en: There was even a juror who had to be excused one day.
sentences.zh: 甚至有一天还有一个陪审员不得不请假。

sentences.en: They had to take a break in the trial because she got sick and she told the judge that she couldn't sleep, that, you know, she'd been up until 2 a.m.
sentences.zh: 审判中不得不暂停，因为她生病了，她告诉法官她睡不着觉，你知道的，她一直醒到凌晨2点，

sentences.en: and she wasn't feeling well.
sentences.zh: 而且她感觉很不舒服。

sentences.en: Regardless of, you know, the nuances of were they an angry mob, were they not?
sentences.zh: 不管那些细微差别如何，你知道的，他们是一群愤怒的暴徒吗，还是说不是？

sentences.en: This was such emotional and powerful testimony that you cannot help but think that that landed well for the prosecution and for the prosecution's case.
sentences.zh: 这是如此情绪化且极具感染力的证词，你不可避免地会认为这对控方以及控方的案子来说效果很好。

sentences.en: But the defense has been able to, in some ways, muddy the waters a little bit, to make it a little bit more complicated and more confusing.
sentences.zh: 但辩方在某种程度上能够把水搅浑一点，让事情变得更复杂、更混乱。

sentences.en: And the defense still has to put on their own witnesses and present their own case.
sentences.zh: 而且辩方还得传唤他们自己的证人并陈述他们自己的案情。

sentences.en: So there's still a long way to go in the trial in that sense.
sentences.zh: 从这个意义上说，审判还有很长的路要走。

sentences.en: But I think as that plays out in the courtroom,
sentences.zh: 但我认为随着案件在法庭上演变，

sentences.en: what's undeniable is that there is a huge unresolved trauma
sentences.zh: 不可否认的是，存在着一个巨大的、尚未解决的创伤，

sentences.en: that so many people have experienced because of this case.
sentences.zh: 由于这个案件，许多人都经历过这种创伤。

sentences.en: should be listed as possible side effects of the vaccine.
sentences.zh: 应被列为该疫苗的可能副作用。

sentences.en: On Wednesday, European regulators described a, quote, possible link between AstraZeneca's COVID-19 vaccine and rare blood clots,
sentences.zh: 周三，欧洲监管机构描述了阿斯利康新冠疫苗与罕见血栓之间，引号中所谓的“可能存在的联系”，

sentences.en: a move that could threaten the pace of vaccinations across Europe and the world.
sentences.zh: 此举可能会威胁到欧洲乃至全球的疫苗接种速度。

sentences.en: This vaccine has proven to be highly effective.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这种疫苗非常有效。

sentences.en: It prevents severe disease and hospitalization, and it is saving lives.

sentences.en: But the regulators emphasized that the benefits of getting the vaccine still outweigh its risks,
sentences.zh: 但监管机构强调，接种疫苗的好处仍然大于风险，

sentences.en: and stopped short of advising that use of the vaccine be curbed in the European Union's 27 countries.
